originalTitle: Morning Mail: Democracy under threat, governor general warns, Europe to boycott Fifa, fires force Clooneys to evacuate
summary: Australia faces ‘catastrophe’ unless people show more understanding of the constitution, Sam Mostyn says; world football splits over selloff plan
content: Good morning. Australia faces a “growing catastrophe” from poor understanding of the country’s constitutional foundation, the governor general, Sam Mostyn, has warned as attacks on institutions and threats against elected officials undermine democratic participation. In other news, European football federations have agreed to boycott Fifa competitions over its selloff plans, George and Amal Clooney have evacuated their home in France, and a library book has been returned after 150 years. Australia Archibald winner | An artist’s portrayal of a Jewish leader produced just weeks after the Bondi massacre has won the Archibald people’s choice category. ‘Lack of understanding’ | The governor general, Sam Mostyn, has said that knowledge of how the country’s system of government operates is in steady decline and better civics education is needed. Liberals at war | The NSW Icac hearings continue to paint the party in a poor light – and the evidence so far has made Angus Taylor’s colleagues anxious. ‘Kmart Keating’? | Ben Carroll’s rise to the premiership in Victoria means Labor’s right faction is in power for the first time since 2010. So where will he lead the state? Borrowed time | An Australian public library has had a book returned an estimated 150 years late after being found behind a wall during a home renovation. World Europe fires | George and Amal Clooney have been forced to evacuate their home in south-eastern France as a wildfire burned nearby. Firefighters tackled a blaze on heath land in Suffolk as England headed for a record number of heat-related deaths after weeks of high temperatures. Check out our visual guide to Europe’s fires. Fifa boycott | European countries have agreed to boycott all Fifa competitions if Gianni Infantino pushes forward with his proposals to sell chunks of the World Cup to US-based private investment. Our exclusive reveals Infantino’s financial prospectus for the game. Football Australia has pleaded for more time to consider the plan while the Asian Football Confederation has accused Fifa of undermining the foundations of football. Middle East | Saudi Arabia is preparing for a major military offensive against the Houthis by sea and possibly by land in central Yemen as the Middle East conflict continues to spiral. Three-quarters of Americans believe Donald Trump is not paying enough attention to the country’s most important problems, according to a new poll. Map mistake | A US government map of Africa mislabelled every country during a state department presentation at a ⁠global conference in Brazil ⁠this week, causing a stir among attenders who took screenshots and posted them online. Brexit bungle | Two Polish citizens who have lived in the UK for nearly 80 years have spoken of their terrifying experience after being told by Ryanair staff at Krakow airport they did not have post-Brexit rights to return to the UK. Full Story Newsroom Edition: ‘shit sheets’ and political scandals Josephine Tovey is joined by Mike Ticher, Patrick Keneally and Anne Davies to talk about a bad week for trust in politics. In-depth Kristen Kappel works as a voluntary assisted dying care navigator as part of a service set up when Victoria became the first state to legislate access in 2019. She tells Stephanie Convery that although it can be stressful and intense, the team sees “a lot of love. I think you carry a little bit of just about everyone with you.” Not the news Reflecting on a family holiday in Europe and a trip to London Zoo, the writer James Colley risks the wrath of zoo lovers by observing that the “simple fact of the matter is there is no point visiting a zoo in another city, or another country”. Sport Commonwealth Games | Australia’s team pursuiters have had mixed fortunes on day one of the track cycling with Australia’s men losing gold to England, while the women’s team beat New Zealand to the title. Organisers have dismissed claims by Idi Amin’s grandson of corruption and racism after he was disqualified for a head-butt in the super-heavyweight boxing. Cricket | Former New Zealand Test captain Stephen Fleming has been confirmed as the new coach of the England men’s Test team, while Joe Root will return for a second spell as captain. AFLW | Tomorrow’s sold-out AFLW All-Stars game offers a chance to celebrate how Irish players have shaped the game with 46 Irish players on current team lists. Media roundup Economists tell the Financial Review that Australia still faces rate hikes this year despite this week’s inflation report. Three state health ministers have publicly revolted against the plan to scrap higher private health insurance rebates for over-65s, according to the Australian. The Tasmanian government has backtracked on a plan for a “Bunnings-style” car park at the entrance to Freycinet national park, the Mercury reports. Golf superstar Rory McIlroy will play at Victoria’s Cathedral Invitational this summer in a major coup for the Australian circuit, the Age reports. What’s happening today Victoria | A remembrance ceremony will take place for 13-year-old Layla Jeffery in Donald. Art | Hadley’s art prize winner will be announced. chineseTitle: 早间邮报：总督警告民主受到威胁，欧洲抵制国际足联，火灾迫使克鲁尼撤离
chineseSummary: 萨姆·莫斯廷说，除非人们对宪法表现出更多的理解，否则澳大利亚将面临“灾难”；世界足坛因抛售计划出现分歧
chineseContent: 早上好。总督萨姆·莫斯廷警告说，由于对该国宪法基础缺乏了解，澳大利亚面临着一场“日益严重的灾难”，因为对机构的攻击和对民选官员的威胁破坏了民主参与。其他新闻方面，欧洲足球联合会已同意抵制国际足联的抛售计划，乔治·克鲁尼和阿迈勒·克鲁尼已撤离法国的家，图书馆的一本藏书在 150 年后被归还。澳大利亚阿奇博尔德获奖者 |邦迪大屠杀几周后，一位艺术家对犹太领袖的描绘赢得了阿奇博尔德人民选择奖。 “缺乏理解”|总督萨姆·莫斯廷表示，人们对国家政府体系运作方式的了解正在稳步下降，需要更好的公民教育。 Liberals at war |新南威尔士州廉政公署听证会继续给该党留下不好的印象——迄今为止的证据让安格斯·泰勒的同事们感到焦虑。 ‘Kmart Keating’? |本·卡罗尔 (Ben Carroll) 升任维多利亚州总理意味着工党右翼派系自 2010 年以来首次掌权。那么他将领导该州走向何方呢？ Borrowed time |澳大利亚一家公共图书馆在一次房屋装修过程中在墙后发现了一本书，估计迟到了 150 年才归还。 World Europe fires |由于附近发生野火，乔治·克鲁尼和阿迈勒·克鲁尼被迫撤离法国东南部的家。消防队员在萨福克郡的荒野上扑灭大火，英格兰在经历了数周的高温后，与高温相关的死亡人数将创下历史新高。查看我们的欧洲火灾视觉指南。 Fifa boycott |如果詹尼·因凡蒂诺推进他的提议，欧洲国家已同意抵制所有国际足联比赛
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于全球新闻信号，适合用于观察外部环境、政策变化、地缘风险和市场情绪。
